PLEASE REFER TO THE STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT AND ETHICAL EXPECTATIONS FOR COLLEGE OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY STUDENTS FOR SPECIFICS. ** # WESTERN GOVERNORS UNIVERSITY ## D424 – SOFTWARE ENGINEERING CAPSTONE Welcome to Software Engineering Capstone! This is an opportunity for students to develop full stack software engineering documentation and applications. They will execute documentation, unit testing, revision of software applications, and deploy software applications with scripts and containers on a cloud platform. FOR SPECIFIC TASK INSTRUCTIONS AND REQUIREMENTS FOR THIS ASSESSMENT, PLEASE REFER TO THE COURSE PAGE. BASIC INSTRUCTIONS For this assessment, you will deploy your developed full stack software product to a web service of your choice. ## SUPPLEMENTAL RESOURCES 1. How to clone a project to IntelliJ using Git? > Ensure that you have Git installed on your system and that IntelliJ is installed using [Toolbox](https://www.jetbrains.com/toolbox-app/). Make sure that you are using version 2022.3.2. Once this has been confirmed, click the clone button and use the 'IntelliJ IDEA (HTTPS)' button. This will open IntelliJ with a prompt to clone the proejct. Save it in a safe location for the directory and press clone. IntelliJ will prompt you for your credentials. Enter in your WGU Credentials and the project will be cloned onto your local machine. 2. How to create a branch and start Development? - GitLab method > Press the '+' button located near your branch name. In the dropdown list, press the 'New branch' button. This will allow you to create a name for your branch. Once the branch has been named, you can select 'Create Branch' to push the branch to your repository. - IntelliJ method > In IntelliJ, Go to the 'Git' button on the top toolbar. Select the new branch option and create a name for the branch. Make sure checkout branch is selected and press create. You can now add a commit message and push the new branch to the local repo. ## SUPPORT If you need additional support, please navigate to the course page and reach out to your course instructor. ## FUTURE USE Take this opportunity to create or add to a simple resume portfolio to highlight and showcase your work for future use in career search, experience, and education! ## Kolibri documentation > **Private product baseline:** Kolibri remains private and unlaunched until > graduation. The source and working-tree provenance for this GitHub baseline is > recorded in > [`docs/private-repository-provenance.md`](docs/private-repository-provenance.md). > Deployment workflows are manual-only while this gate is active; pushes to > `main` do not publish images, deploy services, or update the hosted frontend. > **Required Figma authoring gate:** Before generating any new or structurally > changed Design System, run the complete > [`Universal Figma compatibility prompt`](docs/figma-compatibility-prompt.md). > Do not shorten it or replace its predetermined decisions with ad hoc choices. Start with the system documentation: | Document | Covers | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) | Documentation index and end-to-end product workflow. | | [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | System topology, trust boundaries, authentication, ownership, relational schema, secrets, runtime modes, and storage. | | [`docs/api.md`](docs/api.md) | Complete authenticated HTTP/SSE contract, validation, inputs, outputs, errors, history, reports, and dashboard calculations. | | [`docs/generation-pipeline.md`](docs/generation-pipeline.md) | Figma source contract, metadata, normalization, versioning, diagnostics, React/CSS/Storybook generation, artifacts, and npm publication. | | [`docs/component-contracts.md`](docs/component-contracts.md) | Composable generated views, semantic Figma parts, behavior adapters, manifest schema, stability guarantees, and legacy migration. | | [`docs/neutral-contract-release.md`](docs/neutral-contract-release.md) | Private renderer-neutral schema, immutable release bundle, validation command, deterministic fixtures, and compatibility policy. | | [`docs/bleecker-toggle-conformance.md`](docs/bleecker-toggle-conformance.md) | Black-box Bleecker toggle-family proof, expected semantic output, portability decision, and consumer-owned boundaries. | | [`docs/figma-compatibility-prompt.md`](docs/figma-compatibility-prompt.md) | Canonical copy-ready Figma inventory, audit, repair, and validation prompt required before generation. | | [`docs/operations.md`](docs/operations.md) | Configuration, local runtime, AWS/IAM, CI/CD, deployment behavior, smoke tests, backups, and troubleshooting. | | [`backend/README.md`](backend/README.md) | Backend architecture, authenticated generation flow, migrations, runtime variables, secrets, and local execution. | | [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) | Public browser configuration, local development, Cognito callback ownership, and static publishing. | | [`infrastructure/README.md`](infrastructure/README.md) | Complete deployment runbook: Google OAuth, CDK, production PostgreSQL, grants, system-secret JSON, IAM identities, on-premises host, GitHub/GitLab variables, deployment, and smoke testing. | For a technical overview, start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md). For a new production environment, start with the numbered deployment order in [`infrastructure/README.md`](infrastructure/README.md#deployment-order). It is the canonical operations guide; component README files link back to the relevant runbook sections rather than duplicating production credentials or commands. ## Kolibri local development The root `compose.yaml` is for local development only; it is not a production deployment definition. Development uses Dockerized PostgreSQL for application records, SQLite as the local Secrets Manager substitute, and local filesystem artifact storage. Production backend and PostgreSQL services remain on premises and are not provisioned by CDK or Compose. Configuration is owned by the component that consumes it: - `frontend/.env.example` contains only the public Vite API URL, Cognito hosted domain, and Cognito app-client ID. - `backend/.env.example` contains only API, Cognito, and stack-namespace settings. PostgreSQL and production generation-storage configuration belong exclusively in the stack-derived system secret. - `infrastructure/.env.example` contains the canonical Route 53 inputs and deployment-only Google OAuth values used when invoking CDK. There is no shared root environment file. Values that represent the same deployed resource, such as the public Cognito app-client ID, should be copied from the same CDK output into each consuming component's localized environment. 1. Copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env` and `frontend/.env.example` to `frontend/.env.local`. 2. Set the same public Cognito app-client ID in the backend and frontend files, along with their other localized runtime settings. Do not add AWS, Google, Figma, database-production, or other credentials. 3. Validate and start the local stack: ```bash docker compose config docker compose up --build --watch ``` Local nginx exposes the frontend at `https://kolibri.dev`, the API at `https://api.kolibri.dev`, and the public health endpoint at `https://api.kolibri.dev/health`. Compose publishes ports `5188` and `3188` only as nginx upstreams. PostgreSQL migrations run before the API process, and the frontend waits for the backend health check. Compose Watch synchronizes backend `src/` and frontend `app/` or `public/` changes into their development containers. Nest and React Router then reload automatically. Changes to package manifests, Dockerfiles, or framework configuration rebuild only the affected service. Stop the stack with `Ctrl+C`, or run `docker compose down` if it was started in the background. Compose loads the committed sanitized defaults from `backend/.env.example` and `frontend/.env.example`, then overlays the corresponding untracked localized file when present. Application records are stored in PostgreSQL's private `postgres-data` volume. The private `backend-data` volume contains only the SQLite substitutes for the system and shared Design System secrets. Generated snapshots and packages use the private `generation-artifacts` volume. Development does not read Secrets Manager or S3 and does not need AWS credentials. Cognito remains the configured authentication service. Production uses the `KolibriStackName` CDK output and reads PostgreSQL, S3, and runtime configuration through the host's AWS credential chain. To exercise the production runtime-configuration and artifact providers while retaining the development server, set `KOLIBRI_RUNTIME_MODE=production` in `backend/.env` and provide the normal production stack namespace and AWS credential chain. PostgreSQL remains the application database in both modes; production mode obtains its connection from the system secret. Infrastructure deployment configuration remains separate: copy `infrastructure/.env.example` to `infrastructure/.env` only when running CDK commands from that directory. There is intentionally no root environment template. Infrastructure bootstrap, deployment, runtime permissions, and frontend publishing instructions are in `infrastructure/README.md`.

# Kolibri review contract

Kolibri is a private, authenticated design-system compiler: an owner connects a
Figma file, the NestJS backend normalizes tokens, components and variants into a
versioned React/CSS/Storybook package, and the React Router frontend drives that
workflow behind Cognito. The `contract/` package and `conformance/` suite define
the renderer-neutral output contract. Kolibri is private and unlaunched; its
deployment workflows are manual-only and a merge is never a deployment claim.

Preserve owner scoping on every read and write, write-only runtime credentials
(secrets never leave Secrets Manager or the local substitute), explicit failures
instead of silent fallbacks, deterministic generation output, immutable contract
releases, and the documented generation-run lifecycle and event history. The
Universal Figma compatibility prompt is the authoring contract for design
systems; do not weaken it or the compiler boundary it protects.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance serve this existing product without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new tenant or sharing model, a new external publication target,
a change to what credentials the backend may read back, or a new public surface.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation. Changes to review controls, coverage measurement, the immutable
contract release, or this purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Exactly 100% line and branch
coverage of the backend application sources under `backend/src` is the
requirement for automatic approval; the backend measures every `.ts` source
(modules, entities and DTOs included) with no exclusions. Below 100% a change
may still be reviewed, but it stays pending for a human merge. Narrowing or
widening this measurement is a review-control change that requires explicit
owner confirmation.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. All native tests and exact coverage
remain mandatory. Clouseau owns the shared scoring, investigation, repair
bounds, evidence ledger, native approval and auto-merge; this repository owns its
purpose and real tests.

name: Kolibri CI
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('Verify PR #{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) ||
      inputs.check_author && 'Verify repair author' ||
      (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'Verify main' ||
      format('PR review ({0})', github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref_name) }}
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'policy-install/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  pull_request_target:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, edited]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pull_request:
        description: PR number to reassess without executing contributor code; empty runs verification
        type: string
        required: false
      check_author:
        description: Inspect existing repair author identity and repository access without writing or deploying
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: kolibri-ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  resolve-clouseau:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, helix]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.sha }}
      digest: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - id: engine
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@f5b6f04a5b95090fc0b5dc0e6fec85cc426273f0
        with:
          provenance: summary

  verify:
    name: >-
      ${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)) && 'verify' || 'metadata-only' }}
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, helix]
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: &verify-code >-
          github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: *verify-code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Verify the frozen Clouseau engine
        if: *verify-code
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: verify-engine
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        if: *verify-code
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Set up Python for frozen shared tests
        if: *verify-code
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Install frozen shared test dependencies
        if: *verify-code
        run: python3 -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check -r .clouseau-ci/requirements-test.txt
      - name: Test approval policy
        if: *verify-code
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: test
      - name: Test workflow routing
        if: *verify-code
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix .github/tests --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
          npm test --prefix .github/tests
      - name: Install backend dependencies
        if: *verify-code
        run: npm ci --prefix backend
      - name: Build backend
        if: *verify-code
        run: npm run build --prefix backend
      - name: Type-check frontend
        if: *verify-code
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix frontend
          npm run typecheck --prefix frontend
      - name: Test infrastructure
        if: *verify-code
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix infrastructure
          npm test --prefix infrastructure
      - name: Validate and test neutral contract
        if: *verify-code
        run: |
          npm run validate --prefix contract
          npm test --prefix contract
      - name: Run backend tests with source coverage
        if: *verify-code
        run: npm run test:coverage --prefix backend
      - name: Select the accepted base revision and its protected configuration
        if: *verify-code
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: |
          # An empty base (new branch, manual run) leaves the stricter exact 100% gate in force.
          if [[ -z "$BASE_SHA" || "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
            echo "COVERAGE_BASE_SHA=" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            cp .github/clouseau.json "$RUNNER_TEMP/clouseau-base.json"
            exit 0
          fi
          git cat-file -e "$BASE_SHA^{commit}"
          echo "COVERAGE_BASE_SHA=$BASE_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          # The base revision's file is authoritative; only the initial installation, whose base has none, reads this revision's.
          if git cat-file -e "$BASE_SHA:.github/clouseau.json" 2>/dev/null; then
            git show "$BASE_SHA:.github/clouseau.json" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/clouseau-base.json"
          else
            cp .github/clouseau.json "$RUNNER_TEMP/clouseau-base.json"
          fi
      - name: Measure the base revision's native coverage baseline
        if: *verify-code
        env:
          CLOUSEAU_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/.clouseau-ci
        run: |
          # The baseline is measured by running the base revision's own tests, never this pull request's code.
          if [[ -z "$COVERAGE_BASE_SHA" ]]; then exit 0; fi
          git worktree add --detach "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" "$COVERAGE_BASE_SHA"
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/backend"
          npm ci
          # Same command as `npm run test:coverage`, spelled out because the first base predates that script.
          npx jest --coverage --coverageReporters=json --coverageReporters=text-summary --coverageProvider=v8 --testTimeout=30000 --collectCoverageFrom='**/*.ts' --coverageThreshold='{}'
          node "$CLOUSEAU_ROOT/bin/coverage-gate.cjs" totals coverage/coverage-final.json src istanbul > "$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline.json"
      - name: Enforce 100% line and branch coverage
        if: *verify-code
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: coverage
          coverage-format: istanbul
          coverage-report: backend/coverage/coverage-final.json
          source-directory: backend/src
          config: ${{ runner.temp }}/clouseau-base.json
          coverage-base-ref: ${{ env.COVERAGE_BASE_SHA }}
          coverage-baseline: ${{ runner.temp }}/baseline.json

  assess-intent:
    if: &review-event >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
      (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, helix]
    timeout-minutes: 70
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
    outputs:
      assessment: ${{ steps.local-review.outputs.assessment || steps.assess.outputs.assessment }}
      review-record: ${{ steps.local-review.outputs.review-record || steps.assess.outputs.review-record }}
      number: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - name: Verify the owner-authorized frozen reviewer installation
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        id: install
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const match = context.ref.match(/^refs\/heads\/policy-install\/pr-([1-9][0-9]*)$/);
            if (context.actor !== context.repo.owner || !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(context.sha) || !match) {
              throw new Error('Reviewer installation requires the repository owner and a ready PR number');
            }
            const pull_number = Number(match[1]);
            if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pull_number)) throw new Error('Invalid installation PR number');
            const {data: pr} = await github.rest.pulls.get({...context.repo, pull_number});
            if (pr.state !== 'open' || pr.draft || pr.base.ref !== 'main' ||
                pr.user.login !== context.repo.owner || pr.head.sha !== context.sha ||
                pr.head.repo?.full_name !== `${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}`) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires the owner-authored same-repository PR at this exact workflow revision');
            }
            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments,
              {...context.repo, issue_number: pull_number, per_page: 100});
            if (!comments.some(comment => comment.user?.type === 'User' && comment.user.login === context.repo.owner &&
                comment.body.trim() === `/approve-intent ${context.sha}`)) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires owner intent confirmation at this exact revision');
            }
            core.setOutput('number', String(pull_number));
      # Never load the controller or its configuration from the PR.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Wait for tests and exact coverage
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          REQUESTED_PR: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
        with:
          script: |
            const path = require('node:path');
            const root = path.resolve('.clouseau-ci');
            const config = require(path.join(root, 'src/config.cjs')).loadConfig('.github/clouseau.json');
            const policy = require(path.join(root, 'src/policy.cjs')).createPolicy(config, {engine: require(path.join(root, 'src/central-version.cjs')).environmentEngine()});
            const number = context.payload.pull_request?.number || Number(process.env.REQUESTED_PR);
            for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt++) {
              const {data: pr} = await github.rest.pulls.get({...context.repo, pull_number: number});
              const expected = context.payload.pull_request?.head.sha || context.sha;
              if (pr.state !== 'open' || pr.draft || pr.head.sha !== expected) {
                throw new Error('PR closed, became draft, or changed while verification was pending');
              }
              const result = await policy.technicalRun(github, context.repo, pr);
              if (result.failure) throw new Error(result.failure);
              if (!result.pending) { core.info(`Verified PR CI: ${result.url}. Clouseau acceptance can now start.`); return; }
              core.info('Waiting for independent tests and exact coverage. No AI request has been made.');
              await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 15000));
            }
            throw new Error('PR verification did not complete within 30 minutes');
      - name: Select authenticated local review or the installed CI reviewer
        id: review-route
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            core.setOutput('local', String((context.payload.pull_request?.body || '').includes('clouseau-local-review:v1')));
      - name: Verify authenticated local review without AI credentials
        if: steps.review-route.outputs.local == 'true'
        id: local-review
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: verify-local
          record-transport: job-output
          pull-request: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
      - name: Review unstamped PR through the installed CI AI reviewer
        if: steps.review-route.outputs.local != 'true'
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        id: assess
        with:
          operation: assess
          record-transport: job-output
          pull-request: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
          provider-key: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          typesafe-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }}

  approve-and-merge:

name: Deploy frontend

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: frontend-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, helix]
    environment: production
    env:
      AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
      AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
      FRONTEND_BUCKET_NAME: ${{ vars.FRONTEND_BUCKET_NAME }}
      CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID: ${{ vars.CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID }}
      VITE_API_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.VITE_API_BASE_URL }}
      VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN: ${{ vars.VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN }}
      VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - name: Validate deployment configuration
        run: |
          test -n "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"
          test -n "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
          test -n "$AWS_REGION"
          test -n "$FRONTEND_BUCKET_NAME"
          test -n "$CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID"
          test -n "$VITE_API_BASE_URL"
          test -n "$VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN"
          test -n "$VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID"
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci
      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run build
      - name: Publish static files
        run: |
          aws s3 sync frontend/build/client "s3://${FRONTEND_BUCKET_NAME}" \
            --delete \
            --cache-control "no-cache" \
            --only-show-errors
          aws s3 cp frontend/build/client/assets "s3://${FRONTEND_BUCKET_NAME}/assets" \
            --recursive \
            --cache-control "public,max-age=31536000,immutable" \
            --only-show-errors
      - name: Invalidate CloudFront
        run: >-
          aws cloudfront create-invalidation
          --distribution-id "$CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID"
          --paths "/*"

# Operations and deployment

> **Generation preflight:** the saved Figma source must first pass the
> [Universal Figma compatibility prompt](figma-compatibility-prompt.md). A
> successful Figma-side audit does not replace checking the persisted backend
> Diagnostics tab after generation.

The command-level AWS/PostgreSQL production runbook remains
[infrastructure/README.md](../infrastructure/README.md). This document explains
how the operational pieces work together and provides verification and failure
recovery guidance.

## Toolchain

Recommended local tools:

- Node.js 24 and npm;
- Docker Desktop with Compose Watch support;
- AWS CLI v2;
- AWS CDK CLI installed through `infrastructure/node_modules`;
- an AWS account and credentials able to deploy the stack;
- an existing public Route 53 hosted zone;
- a Google Cloud OAuth web client;
- PostgreSQL reachable from the on-premises backend host;
- local nginx and a trusted wildcard development certificate when using
  `https://kolibri.dev` and `https://api.kolibri.dev`.

## Configuration ownership

### Infrastructure `.env`

Consumed only by local CDK commands:

| Variable                     | Required | Meaning                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KOLIBRI_DOMAIN`             | yes      | Existing hosted-zone domain, e.g. `example.com`.           |
| `KOLIBRI_HOSTED_ZONE_ID`     | yes      | Route 53 zone ID.                                          |
| `KOLIBRI_SUBDOMAIN`          | yes      | Single label used to form `<subdomain>.<domain>`.          |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`     | yes      | Google web OAuth client ID for Cognito federation.         |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | yes      | Google web OAuth client secret used during CDK deployment. |

Google values are CDK deployment inputs. They do not belong in either kolibri
runtime secret. Infrastructure always deploys in `us-east-1`, required for the
CloudFront certificate.

### Backend `.env`

| Variable                | Production                    | Meaning                                                              |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PORT`                  | required                      | HTTP listen/container port.                                          |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`  | required                      | Comma-separated exact browser origins.                               |
| `AWS_REGION`            | required                      | Region containing Cognito, S3, and Secrets Manager.                  |
| `COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID`  | required                      | Cognito user pool ID.                                                |
| `COGNITO_APP_CLIENT_ID` | required                      | Public frontend app-client ID.                                       |
| `KOLIBRI_STACK_NAME`    | required                      | Namespace for both secrets and S3 key prefix.                        |
| `KOLIBRI_RUNTIME_MODE`  | optional                      | Explicit `local` or `production`; otherwise derived from `NODE_ENV`. |
| `NODE_ENV`              | production deployment sets it | Selects production providers when no explicit runtime mode exists.   |

Database credentials, S3 bucket, registry, and presigned lifetime are not
backend environment variables. They are loaded from the system secret.

AWS access keys are not application variables. The SDK uses the standard AWS
credential chain. Production mounts the deployment account's AWS config at
`/home/node/.aws:ro`.

### Frontend `.env.local` / CI build variables

All `VITE_*` values are public because Vite embeds them in the static bundle.

| Variable                 | Meaning                                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL`      | Canonical API origin, without a route suffix. |
| `VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN`    | Cognito hosted-domain origin.                 |
| `VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID` | Public app-client ID.                         |

Scopes are fixed by the application to `openid email profile`. Callback and
logout URLs are derived from `window.location.origin`, so they do not need
separate environment variables.

## Local development

### Prepare

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
cp frontend/.env.example frontend/.env.local
```

Set matching local Cognito identifiers. Google/Cognito remain real external
authentication; application persistence, runtime config, and artifacts are
local.

Validate and start:

```bash
docker compose config
docker compose up --build --watch
```

`--watch` matters. The Compose file declares `develop.watch`; ordinary
`docker compose up` does not activate source synchronization. With watch:

- `backend/src` syncs to `/app/src`, and Nest recompiles;
- `frontend/app` and `frontend/public` sync, and Vite reloads;
- package manifests, Dockerfiles, and framework configuration rebuild the
  affected image.

Local services:

| Service    | Compose upstream               | Canonical nginx URL              |
| ---------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| PostgreSQL | internal `postgres:5432`       | Not exposed through nginx.       |
| Frontend   | `http://localhost:5188`        | `https://kolibri.dev`            |
| Backend    | `http://localhost:3188`        | `https://api.kolibri.dev`        |
| Health     | `http://localhost:3188/health` | `https://api.kolibri.dev/health` |

The local nginx configuration must proxy `kolibri.dev` to `5188` and
`api.kolibri.dev` to `3188`, preserve request headers, and use the existing
trusted wildcard development certificate. Vite must allow `kolibri.dev`.

### Local persistence

Docker named volumes:

| Volume                 | Container path             | Contents                                                    |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `postgres-data`        | `/var/lib/postgresql/data` | All application records and migration state.                |
| `backend-data`         | `/app/data`                | Local substitutes for the system and Design System secrets. |
| `generation-artifacts` | `/app/artifacts`           | Raw snapshots, unpacked package files, downloadable ZIPs.   |

The volumes survive container rebuilds and `docker compose down`. Deleting
volumes is destructive and is not part of normal restart/rebuild.

Useful commands:

```bash
docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f backend
docker compose logs -f frontend
docker compose restart backend
docker compose up -d --build backend
docker compose down
```

If source changes do not appear in a running container, confirm the stack was
started with `--watch`; otherwise rebuild the affected service.

### Direct verification

```bash
(cd backend && npm ci && npm run build && npm test -- --runInBand)
(cd frontend && npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm run build)
(cd infrastructure && npm ci && npm run build && npm test -- --runInBand && npx cdk synth)
docker compose config
```

## AWS infrastructure

`npm run deploy` in `infrastructure/` performs:

1. TypeScript build.
2. CDK synth.
3. CDK deploy.
4. System-secret default initialization (`npm.registry`) without overwriting
   existing values.

Provisioned resources:

### Authentication

- Cognito user pool.
- Public frontend app client (no client secret).
- Cognito hosted domain.
- Google identity provider.
- Callback `<fqdn>/auth/callback`.
- Logout `<fqdn>/sign-in?signedOut=1`.

Google Cloud must authorize the Cognito IdP response URL, not the frontend
callback:

```text
https://<cognito-domain>.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/idpresponse
```

The Cognito app client then redirects the browser to the frontend callback.

### Frontend hosting and DNS

- private encrypted S3 frontend bucket;
- CloudFront distribution with Origin Access Control;
- HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect and TLS 1.2 2021 minimum;
- managed security response headers;
- ACM certificate in `us-east-1`;
- Route 53 A and AAAA aliases for `<subdomain>.<domain>`;
- SPA fallback to the static application entry point.

- Frontend must treat the artifact API's JSON as a presigned redirect contract,
  not as ZIP bytes.

### npm publication fails after generation

This is a partial success. Download remains available.

- inspect the persisted `publication_failed` event;
- locate the matching `npm_publication_failed` backend log by `runId`; inspect
  `command`, `exitCode`, `signal`, `stderr`, `stdout`, `errorCode`, and
  `errorStack` after confirming sensitive values appear only as `[REDACTED]`;
- verify npm token presence and permission for the configured package/scope;
- verify system `npm.registry`;
- verify the assigned version is not already published;
- build the downloaded package locally to isolate generated-code failures.

### AWS signature or access denied in CI

- Re-enter access key ID and secret as separate protected secrets without
  surrounding quotes/newlines.
- Validate identity with an action the publisher is supposed to perform (ECR
  login, frontend bucket list, or distribution invalidation), not
  CloudFormation stack inspection.
- Ensure `AWS_REGION` matches the deployed stack.

## Pull request verification and Clouseau review

Every PR runs `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on the Helix self-hosted runners: the
backend build, frontend type-check, infrastructure tests, neutral contract
validation and tests, backend tests with source coverage, and Clouseau's exact
100% line and branch coverage gate over `backend/src`. Run the same commands
locally:

```sh
npm ci --prefix backend && npm run build --prefix backend
npm run test:coverage --prefix backend   # writes backend/coverage/coverage-final.json
```

`test:coverage` measures every backend `.ts` source (no `collectCoverageFrom`
exclusions, no threshold) so the Clouseau gate sees the real inventory. The
repository is below 100% today (recorded baseline: 95.25% lines, 90.73%
branches by Jest, and seven type-only files that Istanbul reports no entry for),
so the coverage step is red and a PR stays pending for a human merge until
coverage reaches 100%. Reviewed PRs carrying a signed local Clouseau receipt
use the CI verifier without provider keys; see `AGENTS.md` and
`.github/clouseau.md` for the purpose contract and the central-source upgrade
model. The CI needs the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` and
`DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN` repository secrets.

Artifact storage and engine bootstrap: the account's Actions artifact quota is
exhausted, so no step uploads or downloads an Actions artifact. `resolve-clouseau`
runs `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve` with `provenance: summary` (the frozen
SHA and digest stay in the run summary), and the review record moves from
assessment to gate and repair as the bounded `review-record` job output
(`record-transport: job-output`). The resolver is pinned to Clouseau `f5b6f04`;
later Clouseau main (`c709020`) has a dangling symlink that breaks action staging
on the Helix runners, so do not move the pin until the owner says it is fixed.

+

+rationale, evidence and `reviewBy` date. An expired exception fails the check, so

evidence.quote: Kolibri issue #4: Pin Kolibri's supported Node runtime and remediate actionable dependency audit findings. Select one supported Node line (24) via .nvmrc and engines.node, use it in all GitHub workflows, remove high/critical npm audit findings in backend, frontend and infrastructure with the smallest compatible lockfile changes (no forced audit rewrite), add a CI audit policy that fails on unreviewed high/critical exposure and records bounded exceptions with owner, evidence and review date, and keep backend/infrastructure/frontend/contract verification green. No product, deployment or contract-release changes.

# Kolibri review contract

Kolibri is a private, authenticated design-system compiler: an owner connects a
Figma file, the NestJS backend normalizes tokens, components and variants into a
versioned React/CSS/Storybook package, and the React Router frontend drives that
workflow behind Cognito. The `contract/` package and `conformance/` suite define
the renderer-neutral output contract. Kolibri is private and unlaunched; its
deployment workflows are manual-only and a merge is never a deployment claim.

Preserve owner scoping on every read and write, write-only runtime credentials
(secrets never leave Secrets Manager or the local substitute), explicit failures
instead of silent fallbacks, deterministic generation output, immutable contract
releases, and the documented generation-run lifecycle and event history. The
Universal Figma compatibility prompt is the authoring contract for design
systems; do not weaken it or the compiler boundary it protects.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance serve this existing product without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new tenant or sharing model, a new external publication target,
a change to what credentials the backend may read back, or a new public surface.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation. Changes to review controls, coverage measurement, the immutable
contract release, or this purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Exactly 100% line and branch
coverage of the backend application sources under `backend/src` is the
requirement for automatic approval; the backend measures every `.ts` source
(modules, entities and DTOs included) with no exclusions. Below 100% a change

# Operations and deployment

> **Generation preflight:** the saved Figma source must first pass the
> [Universal Figma compatibility prompt](figma-compatibility-prompt.md). A
> successful Figma-side audit does not replace checking the persisted backend
> Diagnostics tab after generation.

The command-level AWS/PostgreSQL production runbook remains
[infrastructure/README.md](../infrastructure/README.md). This document explains
how the operational pieces work together and provides verification and failure
recovery guidance.

## Toolchain

Recommended local tools:

- Node.js 24 and npm;
- Docker Desktop with Compose Watch support;
- AWS CLI v2;
- AWS CDK CLI installed through `infrastructure/node_modules`;
- an AWS account and credentials able to deploy the stack;
- an existing public Route 53 hosted zone;
- a Google Cloud OAuth web client;
- PostgreSQL reachable from the on-premises backend host;
- local nginx and a trusted wildcard development certificate when using
  `https://kolibri.dev` and `https://api.kolibri.dev`.

### Node.js runtime and dependency audit

The supported runtime is Node.js 24 (React Router 8 requires 22.22 or newer).
`.nvmrc` is the single source: local version managers read it, every GitHub
workflow passes it to `actions/setup-node`, and the backend, frontend and
infrastructure packages declare `engines.node` (`>=24.0.0 <25`). The backend and
frontend Dockerfiles and the GitLab job already use `node:24` images.

CI runs `node scripts/audit/policy.mjs`, which executes `npm audit` for the
backend, frontend and infrastructure packages. It reports production and
build-only exposure separately. A high or critical advisory fails unless
`scripts/audit/exceptions.json` has a package-specific exception, and every
remaining lower-severity advisory must be covered by an exception with an owner,

rationale, evidence and `reviewBy` date. An expired exception fails the check, so
exceptions are reviewed rather than silently kept. The backend pins `multer` to
2.5.0 through an npm `overrides` entry because `@nestjs/platform-express@11`
bundles 2.4.0, which has a published advisory; Kolibri has no upload route.

## Configuration ownership

### Infrastructure `.env`

Consumed only by local CDK commands:

| Variable                     | Required | Meaning                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KOLIBRI_DOMAIN`             | yes      | Existing hosted-zone domain, e.g. `example.com`.           |
| `KOLIBRI_HOSTED_ZONE_ID`     | yes      | Route 53 zone ID.                                          |
| `KOLIBRI_SUBDOMAIN`          | yes      | Single label used to form `<subdomain>.<domain>`.          |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`     | yes      | Google web OAuth client ID for Cognito federation.         |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | yes      | Google web OAuth client secret used during CDK deployment. |

Google values are CDK deployment inputs. They do not belong in either kolibri

# Kolibri review contract

Kolibri is a private, authenticated design-system compiler: an owner connects a
Figma file, the NestJS backend normalizes tokens, components and variants into a
versioned React/CSS/Storybook package, and the React Router frontend drives that
workflow behind Cognito. The `contract/` package and `conformance/` suite define
the renderer-neutral output contract. Kolibri is private and unlaunched; its
deployment workflows are manual-only and a merge is never a deployment claim.

Preserve owner scoping on every read and write, write-only runtime credentials
(secrets never leave Secrets Manager or the local substitute), explicit failures
instead of silent fallbacks, deterministic generation output, immutable contract
releases, and the documented generation-run lifecycle and event history. The
Universal Figma compatibility prompt is the authoring contract for design
systems; do not weaken it or the compiler boundary it protects.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance serve this existing product without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new tenant or sharing model, a new external publication target,
a change to what credentials the backend may read back, or a new public surface.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation. Changes to review controls, coverage measurement, the immutable
contract release, or this purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Exactly 100% line and branch
coverage of the backend application sources under `backend/src` is the
requirement for automatic approval; the backend measures every `.ts` source

The command-level AWS/PostgreSQL production runbook remains

recovery guidance.

## Toolchain

Recommended local tools:

- Node.js 24 and npm;
- Docker Desktop with Compose Watch support;
- AWS CLI v2;
- AWS CDK CLI installed through `infrastructure/node_modules`;
- an AWS account and credentials able to deploy the stack;
- an existing public Route 53 hosted zone;
- a Google Cloud OAuth web client;
- PostgreSQL reachable from the on-premises backend host;
- local nginx and a trusted wildcard development certificate when using
  `https://kolibri.dev` and `https://api.kolibri.dev`.

## Configuration ownership

### Infrastructure `.env`

Consumed only by local CDK commands:

| Variable                     | Required | Meaning                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KOLIBRI_DOMAIN`             | yes      | Existing hosted-zone domain, e.g. `example.com`.           |
| `KOLIBRI_HOSTED_ZONE_ID`     | yes      | Route 53 zone ID.                                          |
| `KOLIBRI_SUBDOMAIN`          | yes      | Single label used to form `<subdomain>.<domain>`.          |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`     | yes      | Google web OAuth client ID for Cognito federation.         |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | yes      | Google web OAuth client secret used during CDK deployment. |
